+//! The keep law (#1603): the pocket family (2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D
+//! Offset) clears material AROUND a part it must keep, and answers for
+//! that part on the operation itself - whole-model source or stock
+//! source alike - so the verdict never rides on the program sim alone.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own design (`docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`,
+//! the #1603 section) over the sim crate's solid law
+//! (`verify::solid_hits`). No vendor material consulted.
+//!
+//! ## The law
+//!
+//! - **Whole-model source** (`DepthLaw::Keep`): the part's sections are
+//!   islands (#12), so with the default area controls every move stands
+//!   outside the part. An area offset or extension moves the boundary
+//!   INTO those islands, and nothing on the operation judged that. The
+//!   solid law, nothing excused, now runs against the source's own mesh.
+//!   Only where #12's reading applies (`GenJob::around_part`): with no
+//!   stock set up the model is the volume to remove, and nothing is kept.
+//! - **Stock source** (or a pick off the setup's stock): the source is
+//!   the material to remove, but the parts standing inside it are not
+//!   (#1554). The same solid law runs against the setup's parts
+//!   ([`parts_in_stock`]). A document with no part judges nothing.
+//!   #1607 widened this from the pocket family to every 2D kind that
+//!   answers for the part on a part source ([`is_stock_kept_kind`]):
+//!   the typed kinds (Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular), Contour and
+//!   Face take the same solid law; Engrave and Trace take their own
+//!   mark law (`mark_law`) against the parts instead, so a mark on the
+//!   part's surface reads the same whether the line came off the part
+//!   or off the stock. #1631 added the hole kinds (Drill without
+//!   cross holes, Bore, Thread), which take their own containment law
+//!   against the parts - the round wall of a hole the part models where
+//!   the op declares one is excused, nothing else - and the 2D Chamfer,
+//!   which takes the solid law: a stock edge is not a part edge.
+//!   #1635 added the cross drill (a Drill with cross holes,
+//!   [`is_cross_drill`]): its chain answers to its own radial part law
+//!   (`cross_part`) against the setup's parts, as it does against its
+//!   source on a part source - each declared cross hole's round wall,
+//!   about its own axis, excused; never the stock it was read off.
+//!
+//! - **Part source, neighbouring parts** (#1621): a part-source
+//!   operation's own law reads its source's mesh only, so a cut on part
+//!   B that enters part A beside it had no finding on the operation -
+//!   and with the stock turned (the sim refuses to judge) nothing judged
+//!   A at all. Every part-source operation that carries a part law
+//!   (`depth_law_of` not `None`) now also answers to the plain solid law
+//!   against the setup's OTHER parts ([`neighbour_parts`]): no mark
+//!   budget there (a mark is on the part it marks), no hole excused (the
+//!   holes are the source's), nothing kept around. Its own source keeps
+//!   its own law.
+//!
+//! The cutter's own tip and stack are swept against the mesh, so a legal
+//! pocket - its rings tangent to the part - stays clean, and a cut that
+//! enters the part is a blocking `Gouge` on its move.
+
+use crate::geometry::Triangle;
+
+use super::{OpParams, SrcRef};
+
+/// Whether `params` is a pocket-family kind: it clears an area and
+/// keeps the part.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn is_keep_kind(params: &OpParams) -> bool {
+    matches!(params, OpParams::Pocket { .. } | OpParams::Adaptive2D { .. } | OpParams::Offset2D { .. })
+}
+
+/// Whether `params` answers for the parts standing in its stock when
+/// its source is the stock (#1603, #1607, #1631): every 2D kind that
+/// carries a part law on a part source - the pocket family (`Keep`),
+/// Slot, Trochoidal slot and Circular (`authored_law`), Contour and Face
+/// (`Section`), Engrave and Trace (`Mark`), the hole kinds (`Contain`,
+/// [`is_hole_kind`]) - and the 2D Chamfer (#1631: on a part source its
+/// break is the part's own edge; off the stock, the solid law) - and
+/// the cross drill (#1635, [`is_cross_drill`]: `cross_part`).
+#[must_use]
+pub fn is_stock_kept_kind(params: &OpParams) -> bool {
+    is_keep_kind(params)
+        || super::mark_law::is_mark_kind(params)
+        || is_hole_kind(params)
+        || is_cross_drill(params)
+        || matches!(
+            params,
+            OpParams::Slot { .. }
+                | OpParams::TrochoidalSlot { .. }
+                | OpParams::Circular { .. }
+                | OpParams::Contour { .. }
+                | OpParams::Face { .. }
+                | OpParams::Chamfer2D { .. }
+        )
+}
+
+/// Whether `params` is a hole kind that answers to the containment law
+/// (`DepthLaw::Contain`) on a part source: a Drill with no cross holes
+/// (a cross chain answers to `cross_part` against its source), a Bore,
+/// a Thread. Off the stock (#1631) the same law reads the setup's
+/// parts: the drill, bar or mill may enter a part only through a hole
+/// the part models there - its declared hole's round wall excused, to
+/// its diameter and no deeper than its floor - and anywhere else it is
+/// a gouge.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn is_hole_kind(params: &OpParams) -> bool {
+    match params {
+        OpParams::Drill { cross, .. } => cross.is_empty(),
+        OpParams::Bore { .. } | OpParams::Thread { .. } => true,
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+/// Whether `params` is a cross drill: a Drill with cross holes. Its
+/// chain runs along each hole's own axis and answers to `cross_part`
+/// (the cross holes' walls excused about their axes), never to the
+/// vertical-wall containment law; off the stock (#1635) that law reads
+/// the setup's parts ([`parts_in_stock`]) instead of the stock.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn is_cross_drill(params: &OpParams) -> bool {
+    matches!(params, OpParams::Drill { cross, .. } if !cross.is_empty())
+}
+
+/// The parts an operation whose source is NOT the part (the stock, or
+/// picks off it) must still keep: the setup's parts in its frame - what
+/// the program sim judges against (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`:
+/// fixtures and a stock-only model left out). Empty for a kind outside
+/// [`is_stock_kept_kind`], and for a part-solid source (whose own mesh
+/// its `DepthLaw` reads).
+#[must_use]
+pub(super) fn parts_in_stock(
+    world: &flecs_ecs::prelude::World,
+    setup: Option<&str>,
+    params: &OpParams,
+    part_solid: bool,
+) -> Vec<Triangle> {
+    if part_solid || !is_stock_kept_kind(params) {
+        return Vec::new();
+    }
+    crate::setup_align::parts_facets_in(world, setup)
+}
+
+/// The parts a part-source operation must keep beside its own (#1621):
+/// every part the setup holds (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`'s set -
+/// fixtures and a stock-only model left out) but the entities its
+/// source names, in the setup's frame. Empty for a source that is not
+/// the part (whose parts [`parts_in_stock`] reads), for a kind that
+/// carries no part law on a part source, and for a one-part document.
+#[must_use]
+pub(super) fn neighbour_parts(
+    world: &flecs_ecs::prelude::World,
+    setup: Option<&str>,
+    params: &OpParams,
+    src: &SrcRef,
+    part_solid: bool,
+) -> Vec<Triangle> {
+    if !part_solid {
+        return Vec::new();
+    }
+    kept_models(world, params, src, true)
+        .into_iter()
+        .filter_map(|(_, e)| crate::setup_align::facets_in(world, &e, setup))
+        .flatten()
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// The models whose meshes an operation's part laws read beyond its own
+/// source: on a part source ([`neighbour_parts`]) the setup's other
+/// parts, on a stock source ([`parts_in_stock`]) every part. Empty for a
+/// kind that carries no such law.
+fn kept_models(
+    world: &flecs_ecs::prelude::World,
+    params: &OpParams,
+    src: &SrcRef,
+    part_solid: bool,
+) -> Vec<(String, flecs_ecs::prelude::Entity)> {
+    let own: Vec<&str> = match src {
+        _ if !part_solid => {
+            if !is_stock_kept_kind(params) {
+                return Vec::new();
+            }
+            Vec::new()
+        }
+        _ if super::generate::depth_law_of(params, src, true) == super::generate::DepthLaw::None => return Vec::new(),
+        SrcRef::Stock => return Vec::new(),
+        SrcRef::Entity(n) => vec![n.as_str()],
+        SrcRef::Selection(items) => items.iter().map(|g| g.entity.as_str()).collect(),
+    };
+    let skip = crate::stock_source::stock_only_model(world);
+    crate::model::model_entities(world)
+        .into_iter()
+        .filter(|(name, e)| !own.contains(&name.as_str()) && crate::stock_source::judged(world, e, skip))
+        .collect()
+}

+//! The mark law (#1595): the depth law an Engrave or a Trace on the
+//! finished part carries itself, so its verdict never depends on
+//! whether the program sim can model the stock.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own design (`docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`)
+//! over the sim crate's solid law (`verify::solid_hits`, the tool's own
+//! tip and stack swept against the part's mesh); the "wider than deep"
+//! reading of a mark is general machining practice. No vendor material
+//! consulted.
+//!
+//! ## The law
+//!
+//! Both kinds ride the cutter's centre ON a line of the part, so they
+//! enter the part by design and the tangency law stands down
+//! (`Mode::Engrave`). What they may remove is a MARK: under the cutter,
+//! the part's own surface lowered by at most the mark budget:
+//!
+//! `budget = min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`
+//!
+//! That is the depth the operation states, and never deeper than half
+//! the kerf is wide. Anything deeper is a channel, and a channel the
+//! model does not show is a gouge: cut it shallower, or model it (a
+//! modelled groove is the part's own surface, and the law reads it as
+//! such).
+//!
+//! The test is the solid law run against the part LOWERED by the
+//! budget: a cutter that still enters the lowered part stands more than
+//! the budget under the part's surface somewhere beneath it. That
+//! convicts the three things a typed depth can hide - a cut deeper than
+//! a mark, a Top typed below the surface the line lies on, and a wall
+//! standing beside the line above it (the flank cuts it full height) -
+//! and reads the mesh itself, never a lattice. The program sim credits
+//! the same budget under the same cutter ([`budget_of`],
+//! `stock_sim::credit_marks`), so the two judges agree where both speak.
+//!
+//! ## Bounded by the part under the cutter
+//!
+//! Lowering alone lets a part thinner than the budget drop clear of the
+//! cutter - a 2 mm plate under a 2.9 mm "mark" is cut through (review of
+//! PR #1615). So a second reading stands beside it: the cutting edge
+//! may not come within [`MARK_FLOOR`] of an underside of the part - its
+//! bottom, or the roof of a void in it (`verify::seat_skin`, the
+//! undersides raised into a solid the edge may not enter). A mark is
+//! thus never deeper than `min(budget, thickness under the cutter -
+//! MARK_FLOOR)`; past that it is a breakthrough, said by that name.
+//!
+//! ## Only the edge gets the budget
+//!
+//! The budget is the cutting edge's (the fluted length). The shank and
+//! the holder on a cutting move, and the whole assembly on a rapid,
+//! are judged against the part as it stands, not lowered
+//! (`verify::stack_hits`): steel that is not an edge has no mark to
+//! make.
+
+use crate::cl::Toolpath;
+use crate::geometry::{Point3, Triangle};
+use crate::schema::Operation;
+use crate::units::{self, Unit};
+use crate::verify::{self, Warning, MARK_FLOOR};
+
+use super::material::GOUGE_TOL;
+use super::OpParams;
+
+/// The solid law's sample spacing along a vertical-plane arc, mm (the
+/// containment kinds' number; a trace has none, every move is swept
+/// exactly).
+const STEP: f64 = 0.25;
+
+/// The mark budget of a cut from `top` to `bottom` with a cutter of
+/// radius `cutter_r`: the lesser of the two, never negative; zero (no
+/// entry at all is a mark) when a number is not finite.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn budget(top: f64, bottom: f64, cutter_r: f64) -> f64 {
+    if !(top.is_finite() && bottom.is_finite() && cutter_r.is_finite()) {
+        return 0.0;
+    }
+    (top - bottom).min(cutter_r).max(0.0)
+}
+
+/// Whether `params` is a kind the mark law speaks for.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn is_mark_kind(params: &OpParams) -> bool {
+    matches!(params, OpParams::Engrave { .. } | OpParams::Trace { .. })
+}
+
+/// The mark budget operation `op` declares, for the program sim's
+/// credit: `Some` only for an Engrave or Trace (the operations that
+/// carry the law themselves) with heights that resolve. Whatever the
+/// source: on the finished part the law reads that part, on the stock
+/// (or a pick off it) the setup's parts standing in it (#1607,
+/// `keep_law::parts_in_stock`) - the very mesh the sim judges against,
+/// so the two judges agree. Anything else declares no mark and is
+/// judged against the sharp model.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn budget_of(world: &flecs_ecs::prelude::World, op: &Operation, cutter_r: f64) -> Option<f64> {
+    if !is_mark_kind(&op.params) {
+        return None;
+    }
+    let h = super::resolve_params(world, op.setup.as_deref(), Some(&op.src), &op.params).ok()?;
+    let b = budget(h.top?, h.bottom?, cutter_r);
+    (b > 0.0).then_some(b)
+}
+
+/// `facets` lowered by `by` along Z: the part as a mark of that depth
+/// may leave it, read conservatively (every surface lowered, so a wall
+/// keeps its place and only heights give way).
+fn lowered(facets: &[Triangle], by: f64) -> Vec<Triangle> {
+    let down = |p: Point3| Point3::new(p.x, p.y, p.z - by);
+    facets.iter().map(|t| Triangle::new(down(t.a), down(t.b), down(t.c))).collect()
+}
+
+/// What the mark law added to a path's warnings, by reading.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(super) struct Marked {
+    /// Cutting moves whose edge stands more than the budget under the
+    /// part's surface.
+    pub deep: usize,
+    /// Cutting moves whose edge comes within [`MARK_FLOOR`] of an
+    /// underside of the part: through it, or all but.
+    pub through: usize,
+    /// Moves whose shank or holder (or, on a rapid, any of the
+    /// assembly) enters the part as it stands.
+    pub stack: usize,
+}
+
+/// Append the mark law's convictions of `path` (in the frame of
+/// `facets`) that the laws before it did not already report: a cutting
+/// move whose edge stands more than `budget` under the part's surface,
+/// or within [`MARK_FLOOR`] of its underside, is a `Gouge`; one whose
+/// shank or holder enters the part as it stands a `ShankHit` on the
+/// part; a rapid that does a `RapidInStock`. Returns what each reading
+/// found (a move two readings convict is counted under both and
+/// reported once).
+pub(super) fn mark_into(
+    warns: &mut Vec<Warning>,
+    path: &Toolpath,
+    facets: &[Triangle],
+    cutter: &verify::Cutter,
+    budget: f64,
+    excess: f64,
+) -> Marked {
+    let law = verify::SolidLaw {
+        step: STEP,
+        // #864: less a coarse model's excess, while that is honest.
+        allow: verify::excess_floor(GOUGE_TOL, excess).unwrap_or(GOUGE_TOL),
+        hole_walls: false,
+    };
+    let budget = if budget.is_finite() { budget.max(0.0) } else { 0.0 };
+    let is_gouge = |w: &Warning| matches!(w, Warning::Gouge { .. });
+    // The edge against the part lowered by the budget. The stack's
+    // findings there are dropped: it is judged below, unlowered.
+    let deep: Vec<Warning> = verify::solid_hits(path, &lowered(facets, budget), cutter, &law).into_iter().filter(is_gouge).collect();
+    // The edge against the floor the mark must leave on every underside.
+    // A mesh whose undersides cannot be read fails closed in the reading
+    // above (the same vertices), so nothing is lost by an empty skin.
+    let skin = verify::seat_skin(facets, MARK_FLOOR).unwrap_or_default();
+    let through: Vec<Warning> = verify::solid_hits(path, &skin, cutter, &law).into_iter().filter(is_gouge).collect();
+    // Shank, holder and rapids against the part as it stands.
+    let stack = verify::stack_hits(path, facets, cutter, &law);
+    let found = Marked { deep: deep.len(), through: through.len(), stack: stack.len() };
+    for w in deep.into_iter().chain(through).chain(stack) {
+        if !warns.contains(&w) {
+            warns.push(w);
+        }
+    }
+    found
+}
+
+/// The notes a path carries for what the mark law convicted: the
+/// budget and the floor by name and what to do about each (the warnings
+/// say where). A stack finding carries its own message and no note.
+#[must_use]
+pub(super) fn notes(kind: &str, found: Marked, budget: f64, unit: Unit) -> Vec<String> {
+    let mut out = Vec::new();
+    if found.deep > 0 {
+        out.push(note(kind, budget, unit));
+    }
+    if found.through > 0 {
+        out.push(through_note(kind, unit));
+    }
+    out
+}
+
+/// The note for a cut deeper than a mark: the budget by name.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn note(kind: &str, budget: f64, unit: Unit) -> String {
+    format!(
+        "{kind} cuts deeper than a mark: the cutter stands more than {} {} under the part's surface \
+         (the mark budget: the lesser of Top - Bottom and the cutter radius) - cut shallower, raise Top \
+         to the surface the line lies on, or model the groove",
+        units::len(budget, unit, 3),
+        unit.suffix()
+    )
+}
+
+/// The note for a breakthrough: the floor by name.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn through_note(kind: &str, unit: Unit) -> String {
+    format!(
+        "{kind} cuts through the part: under the cutter less than {} {} of the part is left on its underside \
+         (a mark is bounded by the part under it, less that floor) - cut shallower; a cut through the part is \
+         not a mark",
+        units::len(MARK_FLOOR, unit, 3),
+        unit.suffix()
+    )
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+#[path = "mark_law_tests.rs"]
+mod tests;

+//! The marks the program declares (#1595): the program sim credits an
+//! Engrave's or a Trace's cut into the finished part only as the mark
+//! its OWN operation carries a law for - its cutter's sweep, no deeper
+//! than the operation's mark budget (`operation::mark_law`). The budget
+//! is computed here from the operation's parameters and tool as they
+//! stand, never read from a cached record, so file data cannot state a
+//! deeper mark than the operation does (the #529 bound, by
+//! construction). An operation on any other kind declares no mark and
+//! is judged against the sharp model - stricter, never looser. Since
+//! #1607 a stock-source Engrave or Trace declares its mark too: its
+//! operation holds it to the same budget against the setup's parts.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own wiring of this repo's mark law onto the sim
+//! crate's `credit_marks`. No vendor material consulted.
+
+use super::Planned;
+use crate::stock_sim::{Mark, SimOp};
+
+/// The marks the program declares, in the frame the verdict is read in:
+/// every op's when one frame holds the whole program, only the final
+/// frame's ops' when the program spans setups that hold the part
+/// differently (the rule `program_breaks` keeps for the edge breaks).
+pub(super) fn program_marks<'a>(
+    world: &flecs_ecs::prelude::World,
+    planned: &'a [Planned],
+    spanned: bool,
+    frame: &Option<String>,
+) -> Vec<Mark<'a>> {
+    planned
+        .iter()
+        .filter(|p| !spanned || crate::setup::effective(world, p.setup.as_deref()) == *frame)
+        .filter_map(|p| {
+            let budget = p.mark?;
+            Some(Mark { op: SimOp { moves: &p.moves, radius: p.radius, ball: p.ball, cone: p.cone, corner: p.corner }, budget })
+        })
+        .collect()
+}

+## #1595 - An Engrave or Trace on the finished part answers to a mark law of its own
+
+**Decided:** `depth_law_of` gives `OpParams::Engrave` and
+`OpParams::Trace` a new `DepthLaw::Mark` whenever the source is the
+finished part, whole model or pick (`crates/app/src/operation/mark_law.rs`).
+The law: under the cutter, the part's own surface may give way by the
+**mark budget** and no more,
+
+    budget = min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)
+
+It is tested with the existing solid law (`verify::solid_hits`, the
+tool's own tip and stack swept against the mesh) run against the part
+LOWERED by the budget. A cutting move whose edge still enters the
+lowered part is a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on that move; the path also
+carries a note that names the budget and what to do. A source that is
+not the part (the Stock, or a pick off the setup's stock) is still
+`None`, as for every kind. (Amended by the review of PR #1615, below:
+the mark is also bounded by the part under the cutter, and the shank,
+holder and rapids are judged against the part as it stands.)
+
+The program sim credits the same thing (`stock_sim::credit_marks`,
+called beside #303's `credit_breaks`): a column the mark's own cutter
+swept is judged against `max(what that cutter swept, model top -
+budget, underside + 0.2 mm)` instead of the model's top. So the two judges agree where both
+speak, and the operation's verdict stands alone where the sim refuses
+(a turned stock, posed moves, rotary and lathe frames).
+
+**Why a new law:** both kinds ride the cutter's centre ON a line of the
+part, so `Section` would convict every legal engraving, and `None` left
+them with no judge. Measured on the #1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block,
+R15 pocket to Z4, 6 mm end mill), whole-model source, before this
+change:
+
+| cut (Top 8) | stock aligned | stock turned |
+|---|---|---|
+| 0.02 mm deep | refused by the sim ("worst 0.02 mm") | posts |
+| 0.3 mm deep | refused by the sim | posts |
+| 7 mm deep (the issue's repro) | refused by the sim | **posts** |
+
+Both columns were wrong: no engraving on a model could post on an
+aligned stock, and any depth posted on a turned one. After:
+
+| cut (Top 8 unless said) | op gouges | aligned | turned |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 0.02, 0.3, 1, 3 mm deep | 0 | posts | posts |
+| 3.1 mm deep | yes | refused | refused, by the op's moves |
+| 4 mm, 4.1 mm, 7 mm deep | 258-516 | refused | refused, by the op's moves |
+| Top typed 7 (surface at 8), 0.3 stated | yes | refused (charged 1.0) | refused |
+| pocket floor picked, 0.3 deep along the wall's foot | yes | refused | refused |
+
+**What the budget is, and why two terms:**
+- `Top - Bottom` is the depth the operation states. Lowering the part by
+  it asks one question: would the cutter standing at Top touch the part?
+  That convicts what a typed depth can hide - a Top typed below the
+  surface the line lies on, and a wall standing beside the line (a
+  picked pocket floor is traced along the wall's foot, and the flank
+  takes the cutter radius off that wall for its whole height).
+- The cutter radius caps it. The stated depth cannot be the whole
+  budget: the seeded Engrave and Trace carry the job's generic Top and
+  Bottom, so an unedited one runs the full height of the part (the
+  issue's repro), and nothing typed says that is wanted. A kerf deeper
+  than half its width is a channel, not a mark, and a channel the model
+  does not show is a gouge by the same reading #1593 gave the typed
+  slot. The cap is also where a ball's groove stops being its tip form
+  and gains straight walls.
+- The way out for a deliberate deep groove is to model it: a modelled
+  groove is the part's own surface, the budget is measured from its
+  floor, and the cut passes.
+
+**`uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs): left as it is.** Both issues asked
+whether it should stop counting an op at `None` on a model source as
+judged when the sim refuses to judge. Measured against the rule's own
+test - a legal program must still post on a turned stock:
+- Before this PR a legal whole-model Pocket, Adaptive2D and Offset2D
+  were at `None`. The rule would refuse every one of them on a turned
+  stock, a 3+2 frame or a rotary: a false refusal, so those ops needed
+  a law of their own instead (#1603, below).
+- It keeps the verdict tied to whether the sim can model the stock,
+  which is what #1595 asks to remove.
+- It cannot name the move. The op-level laws do.
+- With `Mark` and `Keep`, the only 2D kind left at `None` on a model
+  source is the 2D Chamfer, whose depth is derived and whose break the
+  sim credits (#303). A rule for one kind that is legal by construction
+  would only add refusals.
+
+**Considered and dropped:**

+## #1635 - A stock-source cross drill answers for the parts in its stock
+
+**Reproduced first; not a P1.** #1635 asked whether a stock-source cross
+drill (a Drill with cross holes, source Stock) that enters a part posts
+unjudged. It does not: `cross_part::part_clear` read the source's mesh,
+which off the stock is the stock itself, so EVERY stock-source cross
+drill was refused at generation - into the part and legal alike - with
+"cross hole ... rapids into the finished part: the finished part stands
+in the drill's path". The stock was read as the solid to keep. Nothing
+reached the post; the defect is a false refusal of legal programs (and a
+misleading message), P3 by the AGENTS.md table. The issue keeps its P1
+label until the maintainer lowers it (agents only raise).
+
+**Readings** (measured on 881f7726 and on this branch; the #117 punched
+bar, r10, z [-80, 20], one r2 hole plunging -X from (10, 0, 0) 6 mm deep;
+DR-0400 long series; stocks: an r20 bar and a 40 x 40 box over the
+bar's span, each aligned and turned a quarter about Z; mill-turn and
+lathe test benches; stock-source op "S1"):
+
+| case | before (all four stocks) | now |
+|---|---|---|
+| hole where the bar models none | refused: "rapids into the finished part" (the stock) | refused: "cuts into the finished part: the drill meets steel at the mouth - the model has no hole there" |
+| hole into the bar's modelled hole | refused, the same words | generates the part source's chain move for move; posts |
+| hole in stock-only material (r3 core) | refused, the same words | generates; posts |
+| part source, the same holes | into-part refused, legal posts | unchanged |
+| lathe, box stock, legal hole | refused: "this part cannot be read as turned" (the box) | generates |
+
+A first cut that only swapped the judged mesh (the parts instead of the
+stock) still refused the legal holes, for a rapid into stock: with the
+stock as the source the standoffs were measured about the stock as if
+it were the part, so the mouths stayed at the declared r10 inside the
+r20 raw bar. Hence the whole reading below, not only the judged mesh.
+
+**Decided:** a stock-source cross drill is the chain a part-source cross
+drill drills in the same raw stock (`cross_spindle::Solids`):
+- the setup's parts (`keep_law::parts_in_stock` - fixtures and a
+  stock-only model left out; `keep_law::is_cross_drill` joins
+  `is_stock_kept_kind`) are the solid it measures (`source`) and keeps
+  (`kept`, judged by `cross_part` - each declared cross hole's round
+  wall excused about its own axis, nothing else);
+- the source stock is the raw material (`stock`) its mouths stand off
+  and its rapids are proven clear of (#77, `cross_stock`);
+- on a plain lathe, the parts are the turned work `lathe_reads` reads
+  (a box raw stock is not a turned part).
+
+A setup with no part keeps nothing (`part_clear` returns early on an
+empty mesh); the mouths still stand off the stock.
+
+The vertical-wall laws of the 2D tail (#1607's solid law against the
+setup's parts) skip a cross drill (`parts_crossed`): the radial law
+already judged its chain against the same parts, and the solid law
+with no wall excuse convicts a drill at the size of a faceted cross
+hole (measured: mutation M5).
+
+**Why the part source's law, not a new one:** the issue's "Done means"
+and #1631's reasoning - a hole off the stock is legal in the part only
+where the part has that hole, which is the question `cross_part` asks
+on a part source. Reusing it makes a stock-source cross drill read
+exactly as the same drill on the part (pinned: the chains are equal).

+  hole-kind law): it excuses vertical hole walls only (`HoleAxis`
+  vertical); a cross hole's wall runs along X or Y.
+- Refusing every stock-source cross drill by name: the legal program
+  (drill the part's own cross hole off the raw bar) is common.
